props.title: L'Avventura
props.initialSlug: Mysterious disappearance leads to existential exploration

sections.content: L'Avventura revolutionized cinema by deliberately subverting narrative expectations. Michelangelo Antonioni crafts a mystery about a woman's disappearance, then boldly abandons the mystery entirely to explore emotional alienation and modern ennui. The film's languid pacing, stark compositions, and focus on architectural spaces rather than traditional plot points sparked outrage at Cannes but influenced generations of filmmakers. Like Last Year at Marienbad (1961) and La Notte (1961), it rejected conventional storytelling for psychological exploration.

sections.content: Antonioni's influence echoes through art house cinema, from The Passenger (1975) to Lost in Translation (2003). His technique of using landscape as psychological metaphor and allowing the camera to linger after characters exit the frame became signatures of European modernist cinema. The film's emphasis on wealthy characters trapped in spiritual emptiness prefigured later works like La Dolce Vita (1960) and contemporary examinations of privilege like The Great Beauty (2013).

The film's revolutionary approach to time and narrative continues to influence contemporary cinema. Directors like Michael Haneke, with Code Unknown (2000), and Apichatpong Weerasethakul, with Syndromes and a Century (2006), build on Antonioni's rejection of traditional plot resolution. The film's exploration of female psychology and modern alienation finds echoes in works like Under the Skin (2013) and Portrait of a Lady on Fire (2019). SUBHEAD: Impact on Modern Cinema

sections.content: L'Avventura's visual grammar - emphasizing architecture, negative space, and human insignificance against landscape - influenced filmmakers from Andrei Tarkovsky to Sofia Coppola. The film's treatment of wealthy leisure class ennui created a template for examining privilege and emptiness, seen in works like The Square (2017) and Somewhere (2010). Its radical narrative structure, which privileges mood and atmosphere over plot, paved the way for contemporary slow cinema movements.
